subject: Halcyon RFI: network zoning, containment mapping & threat synthesis
body:
From: Danielle Park <dpark@halcyonsec.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: RFI follow-up: network zoning, containment mapping & threat synthesis

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the high-level packet yesterday. Halcyon's security team has a few targeted asks so we can complete our architecture review:

1) A single-page network zoning diagram that shows control plane / data plane demarcation, operator egress paths, and default egress posture for hosted vs private deployments.
2) A blast-radius matrix mapping failure modes (sidecar compromise, KV cache poisoning, operator lateral movement) to mitigations and recovery steps.
3) A short threat-model summary (3–5 top attack paths) and which controls would be in-scope for SOC2 evidence.

Two clarifying items: does your sidecar model permit host-network egress for inference nodes, and can you describe the default behavior for prefix/KV cache eviction when a tenant is pinned?

Can you get us a concise packet and a point person? Halcyon's deadline is 2026-07-07 for our security committee.

Appreciate it —
Danielle Park
Security Architect, Halcyon Analytics
security@halcyonsec.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Danielle Park <dpark@halcyonsec.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 11:05 AM PDT
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: network zoning, containment mapping & threat synthesis

Danielle —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached are three artifacts that address each item directly:
- redwood_network_zones_v2.drawio.png — single-page zoning diagram (hosted/dedicated/private overlays).
- blast_radius_matrix.xlsx — failure modes vs mitigations.
- threat_model_summary.pdf — concise top-5 attack paths and mapping to SOC2 evidence.

Short answers to your clarifying items:
- Sidecar egress: by default our inference sidecars run in a separate namespace with very restrictive egress rules. For hosted deployments we use an egress-proxy subnet with explicit allowlists; host-network egress is disabled unless the customer requests a private deployment with a specific operator mode.
- KV / prefix cache eviction: tenant-pinned models retain KV prefixes for 10 minutes by default; eviction is LRU within the model-serving process and we never spill tenant KV to shared disk. For customers requiring stricter bounds we can reduce the retention window or enable per-tenant in-memory quotas.

Olga (cc'd) drafted the threat synthesis and contributed the updated zoning diagram — tagging for any technical gaps. Marissa is our compliance lead and can surface what we typically include in a SOC2 evidence packet.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_network_zones_v2.drawio.png, blast_radius_matrix.xlsx, threat_model_summary.pdf

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Danielle Park <dpark@halcyonsec.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 2:30 PM PDT
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: network zoning, containment mapping & threat synthesis

Danielle / Ben —

A few implementation notes to call out for the committee (summarized):

1) Control plane demarcation
- Control plane (orchestration, model registry, rollout) is on a separate VPC/VNet with mutual TLS to the customer-facing data plane. Customers using Redwood Private can opt to host a local control plane with identical API surfaces.

2) Data plane isolation patterns
- Tenant traffic is isolated at three layers: model routing (per-tenant routing table), per-tenant in-memory KV segmentation, and network ACLs at the pod/subnet level.
- No tenant data is written to shared persistent storage by default; logs are streamed to tenant-scoped collectors.

3) Operator/agent breakout scenarios and mitigations
- Operators do not have direct tenant VM access; operator actions go through an RBAC gateway with recorded session and ephemeral certificates.
- Egress from operator tooling is only to monitored update endpoints; all packages are checksummed, and we maintain attestations signed by our build system.

4) KV cache poisoning / prefix abuse
- We detect anomalous prefix divergence using a probabilistic checksum sampling process that compares output histograms across replica sets; suspected poisoning triggers rate-limiting and a forced rehydrate.

5) Failure/recovery choreography
- For sidecar compromise we have an automated circuit breaker that isolates the node and re-routes traffic to warm spare pools. Remediation is staged: isolate -> forensics snapshot -> failover to pinned spare -> rebuild image.

If Halcyon wants, we can expand any of these into playbooks for the audit packet.

- Olga
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@cirrusbank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Danielle Park <dpark@halcyonsec.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 09:00 AM PDT
Subject: A couple of quick clarifications on the diagram

Ben / Olga —

Thanks for the packet. Two quick clarifications from our side:
1) In the zoning diagram, can you annotate the default encryption boundaries (in-transit + at-rest per zone)?
2) Is the sidecar-to-inference node communication mutual-TLS or mTLS + pinning to instance identity? If the latter, do you have an identity provider you integrate with (IdP metadata would be helpful).

Also, can you confirm whether the warm spare pools are in the same availability domain as the primary or cross-AZ by default?

Cheers,
Tom
Senior Cloud Architect, Cirrus Bank

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@cirrusbank.com>, Danielle Park <dpark@halcyonsec.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 04:04 PM PDT
Subject: Re: A couple of quick clarifications on the diagram

Tom / Danielle —

Answers inline:
1) Encryption boundaries — annotated in redwood_network_zones_v2.drawio.png (attached). By default: all inter-zone traffic is encrypted in transit (mutual TLS between zones + per-connection ephemeral keys). At-rest: tenant data in transit buffers and telemetry is encrypted with service-managed keys; for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

2) Sidecar communication — mutual TLS with instance identities; we pin to instance certificate chain plus short-lived attestation tokens issued by our control plane CA. For integrations we support OIDC metadata and can accept IdPs that issue compatible client certificates or federated tokens.

3) Warm spare pools — default is cross-AZ within the same region (failure domain isolation). For ultra-low-latency customers we provide same-AZ spares as an option.

Next steps: Marissa will pull together the SOC2 evidence checklist mapping (artifact names, retention periods) and place the items in the Drive folder linked above. Olga and I can also produce a short playbook on operator breakout remediation if the committee requests it.

Let us know if you want a 30-min walkthrough this week.

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
